subject: RE: Greenline — temporary uptime exception + one-time credit
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Service terms question — temporary uptime target and one-time credit

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We shipped a short pilot and noticed two items we need to reconcile before committing to the annual contract: 

1) Uptime/SLO: our internal security team needs a 99.95% uptime target for production inference endpoints (current template is 99.9%).
2) Commercial: because this is a healthcare workload and we’re moving a portion of traffic over in month 1, we’re asking for a one-time onboarding credit that offsets the ramp risk while we validate throughput.

Attached is a short note from our procurement with the request and a simple table of expected traffic for month 1. Can Redwood provide either a concession on the uptime target (temporary exception) or an alternate remedy (increased service credit) plus a one-time credit on month 1?

If it helps, we can accept a timeboxed exception (90 days) that reverts to the standard SLA after the ramp. Please let me know next steps and who from your side should own this.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Patel
Head of Platform — Greenline Health

Attachment: greenline_sla_request.pdf (1 page PDF, request summary)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aisha Patel <aisha@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-01-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Service terms question — temporary uptime target and one-time credit

Ben / Jonas — forwarding Greenline’s request. Short summary: they need 99.95% for production (template is 99.9%) and would like a one-time onboarding credit to cover month-1 ramp risk. They’re open to a 90-day timeboxed exception that reverts to our standard 99.9% after.

Questions for deal desk / ops:
- What does a temporary 99.95% commitment look like operationally (impact on remedies/service credit buckets)?
- If we can’t change the uptime commitment, can we offer an enhanced service credit schedule or a one-time commercial credit instead? If so, what’s reasonable?

Ben — can you run numbers on a one-time credit that’s equivalent to the incremental risk for the first month (see attached proposed_credit_calc.xlsx)? Jonas — would need your ops perspective on whether we can accept a timeboxed exception and what mitigations you’d want in the contract (e.g., accelerated incident reporting, dedicated SRE onboarding hours).

I’d like to respond to Greenline by EOD Tuesday with either an approval path or a clear counter. Thanks.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of SMB Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_credit_calc.xlsx (Excel, cost/credit calc)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Service terms question — temporary uptime target and one-time credit

Marissa — I ran preliminary numbers based on their projected month-1 RPS and token volume. Two viable options come back: 

Option A (commercial credit): one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month-1 committed spend (~$24k) — easiest commercially, no SLA change.
Option B (SLA concession + reduced credit): accept a 90-day exception to 99.95% but require an elevated service credit cap for that period (double our standard credit) and a smaller onboarding credit (~$10k).

Notes: 
- Option B requires signoff from Ops on tolerable risk and a clause that the exception auto-reverts after 90 days.
- Either option needs Deal Desk approval for the credit line (above standard thresholds) and Exec sign-off for SLA modification.

Attaching my calculation sheet and a suggested clause for a timeboxed exception. If Jonas is comfortable with Option B operationally, I recommend that — it preserves higher uptime nominally while giving them stronger financial remedy if we miss. If Ops is uncomfortable, Option A keeps terms standard and is simpler to approve.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations

Attachment: ben_credit_notes.pdf (1 page — calc highlights)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Service terms question — temporary uptime target and one-time credit

Marissa / Ben — Ops perspective: we can accept Option B with conditions. Key operational asks: 
- 90-day exception window only, after which SLA returns to 99.9% automatically.
- For the 90-day window, if uptime dips below 99.95% we’ll pay double the normal service credit rate (capped at 5% of monthly recurring revenue).
- Greenline must agree to a quick onboarding SRE engagement: 8 hours executed within the first 14 days (covered by Redwood at no additional billing) and a weekly sync during the window.
- Add an accelerated incident notification timeline for the exception window (15 minutes pager vs. standard 30).

If Deal Desk approves the reduced credit and the one-time onboarding credit Ben proposed (~$10k), I’m OK escalating to Exec for final sign-off. Please include these operational clauses in the legal redline.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Platform Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@greenlinehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-14T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Greenline — temporary uptime exception + one-time credit

Hi Aisha — thanks for the patience. Good news: Redwood can accommodate a timeboxed operational concession with a paired commercial credit. Summary of the approved path below.

What we can offer (approved by Deal Desk + Ops, pending standard contract redline):
- Timeboxed SLA exception: 99.95% uptime for 90 days from the production go-live date. After 90 days the SLA will revert to our standard 99.9% automatically.
- Enhanced remedy during exception window: service credit rate = 2x standard (capped at 5% of monthly recurring revenue) if uptime falls below 99.95% during the window.
- One-time onboarding credit: $10,000 applied to month 1 invoice.
- Operational mitigations: 8 hours of SRE onboarding support (no charge) within first 14 days and weekly syncs for the 90-day window. Accelerated incident notifications (15-minute pager).

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll ask Legal to produce a short amendment with the timeboxed language and credit numbers — target draft ready by Friday morning.
2) Procurement to confirm the final go-live date so we can start the 90-day window.
3) Ben will include the credit in the sales order and route the deal for final financial approval.

If that all works, we’ll treat this as a one-off concession scoped to this deal and documented in an amendment. Let me know if Procurement needs anything else.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of SMB Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: greenline_sla_amendment_draft_placeholder.txt (placeholder — final legal redline pending)
